keyAndScale.modalCharacter: A Mixolydian high-energy pub rock driven by an open A pedal bass, ♭VII (G), and IV (D) power chord stabs

scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C# - D - E - F# - G
scalesUsed.application: Underpins the iconic driving verse riff, incorporating the flat-7th (G) for rebellious pub rock swagger
Drives the biting, aggressive blues-rock solo with double-stops and high-energy fretboard stabs
Blended into lead fills to outline the major 3rd (C#) during chorus turnaround hooks

mainProgression.description: High-octane Australian pub rock engine fueled by rapid eighth-note downstrokes and syncopated upbeat accents

sectionProgressions.description: Explosive four-on-the-floor opening establishing the furious 154 BPM tempo and twin-guitar attack
Tight palm-muted open A pedal chug alternating with sharp syncopated chord stabs and dominant V turnaround
Unrestrained full-power pub anthem cadence designed for explosive audience shout-along energy
Rhythm section lays down an uncompromising hard rock groove supporting screaming pentatonic lead lines

harmonicFunction: A5 (Tonic I): Relentless tonal anchor driven by furious open 5th-string downstroke chugging
G5 (Subtonic ♭VII): Injects the raw Mixolydian bite that defines the classic Australian pub rock sound
D5 (Subdominant IV): Uplifting resolution step that propels the riff dynamically back toward the tonic
E5 (Dominant V): Builds the pre-chorus and solo climax tension before slamming into the A5 home root

techniques.name: High-Speed Downstroke Chugging
techniques.description: Executing continuous, machine-gun 154 BPM eighth-note downstrokes with percussive right-hand palm muting

notes: Lock the heel of your picking palm across the lower strings right at the bridge saddles
Keep your wrist loose and bouncy; avoid forearm tension at 154 BPM
Dig in with a heavy plectrum (1.0 mm+) for maximum fundamental bite

techniques.name: Syncopated Pub-Rock Chord Stabs
techniques.description: Targeting sharp off-beat accents on the 'and' of beats 2 and 4 to create undeniable danceable forward drive

notes: Release left-hand finger pressure immediately after striking the G5 and D5 chords to choke the sustain
Coordinate the muting between both hands for razor-sharp rhythmic silence
Accentuate the transition into the open A5 downbeat

sections.name: High-Octane Intro Riff
sections.description: The unmistakable opening salvo featuring furious A5 pedal chugging and punchy G5-D5 upbeat punches
notes: Keep the low open A string pulsing at full 154 BPM intensity
Snap to the 3rd fret G5 and open D5 with crisp left-hand muting
Finish with a roaring E5 power chord push into the verse

sections.name: Driving Pub-Rock Verse
sections.description: Rhythm section locks down a tight, percussive groove underneath Brian Nichol's cheeky, energetic vocals
notes: Apply medium palm muting to the repeated A5 power chords
Unmute sharply on the G5 and D5 chord punches
Build picking velocity through the four E5 beats leading to the chorus

sections.name: Explosive Shout Chorus
sections.description: Full-volume arena pub rock power chords ringing wide open with thunderous live crowd anthemic force
notes: Remove all palm muting and strike all chords with maximum headroom
Let the root and fifth ring out with natural Marshall tube saturation
Accentuate beat 1 of each measure to give the rhythm section massive weight

sections.name: Blazing Pentatonic Guitar Solo
sections.description: Stephen 'Fess' Parker's searing lead break packed with classic Chuck Berry-meets-Angus Young pub rock aggression
notes: Start on the 5th-fret A minor pentatonic box with a rapid hammer-on sequence
Execute whole-step bends at the 7th fret of the G string with wide finger vibrato
Finish with punchy double-stops on the 5th fret of the B and high E strings

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul Custom or Fender Stratocaster with bridge humbucker
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker delivering tight, biting midrange and aggressive upper harmonic crunch

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 2203 / JCM800 100W Lead into 4x12 cabinet with Celestion Greenbacks

effects.distortion: Cranked British valve pre-amp crunch boosted with an Ibanez TS808 Tube Screamer
effects.reverb: Tight analog spring reverb or short room ambience
effects.other: Boss GE-7 graphic equalizer boosting 800 Hz for slicing solo projection

beginner.title: Power Chords & Downstroke Stamina
steps: Master the 2-finger A5, G5, D5, and E5 power chord shapes
Practice downstroke chugging at 110 BPM, focusing on even dynamics
Coordinate the transitions between A5 and the syncopated G5-D5 stabs

intermediate.title: Full Performance Speed & Palm Muting
steps: Push tempo up to 154 BPM using a metronome while eliminating forearm tension
Integrate crisp palm muting in the verses with instant unmuted explosions on choruses
Learn the rhythm guitar turnaround leading into the solo

advanced.title: Fess Parker Lead Soloing
steps: Learn the complete guitar solo note-for-note in A Minor Pentatonic
Master the 7th-fret whole-step bends with pitch-perfect intonation
Nail the double-stop rock 'n' roll licks with authentic Australian swagger

commonMistakes: Tensing the right forearm at 154 BPM, which leads to cramping and dragging tempo
Failing to choke the G5 and D5 stabs, creating a muddy wall of sound instead of tight punch
Over-bending the 7th fret G-string bend in the solo
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Chromatic wrist relaxation warm-up at 120 BPM
10 mins: Verse palm-muted downstroke endurance drill at 135 BPM advancing to 154 BPM
10 mins: Off-beat chord stab timing with a metronome clicking on beats 2 and 4
5 mins: Full track playthrough locking into the live Australian pub rock groove
focusAreas: Wrist relaxation during relentless 154 BPM eighth-note downstrokes
Instant dynamic contrast between palm-muted verse and wide-open chorus
Screaming vibrato on the solo double-stop resolutions
metronomeWork: Begin at 120 BPM ensuring all downstrokes land with identical rhythmic spacing
Step up in 5 BPM increments: 130, 140, 148, and finally 154 BPM
Practice with metronome click on beats 2 and 4 to simulate the snare backbeat
